text.title: EARS Requirement Set — Output Contract
text.summary: The artefact this methodology produces: a requirement set in which every item carries an id, a statement, a classified `ears_pattern`, and — when the pattern is `n-a` — a recorded reason. Machine-checkable by the bundled validator.

list.item: f1 — any requirement without an `FR-NNN` / `NFR-NNN` id.
f3 — any `FR-NNN` with `ears_pattern: n-a`. The opt-out is available to NFRs only; an FR that cannot be expressed as a system response to a condition is not a functional requirement.
f4 — any requirement with `ears_pattern: n-a` and no `ears_pattern_na_reason`. Silent opt-out is the failure this field exists to prevent.
f5 — any FR failing EARS classification in an artefact submitted as final, i.e. `ears_violations` containing an `E`-severity code for that id.
f6 — `owner` equal to `team`, `we`, empty or null.

example.code: { "artefact_id": "F-081-checkout-requirements", "version": "1.0.0", "last_reviewed": "2026-08-04", "owner": "@solo-founder", "requirements": [ { "id": "FR-001", "statement": "When a customer submits the checkout form, the payment service shall create a charge intent.", "ears_pattern": "event-driven", "priority": "must", "verification_method": "integration test", "source_flow": "user-flows.md#checkout-happy-path" }, { "id": "FR-002", "statement": "If the payment provider returns a declined status, then the checkout page shall display the message \"Card declined\".", "ears_pattern": "unwanted-behaviour", "priority": "must", "verification_method": "negative test" }, { "id": "NFR-001", "statement": "The billing service shall encrypt stored card tokens at rest using AES-256.", "ears_pattern": "ubiquitous", "priority": "must", "verification_method": "property test + monitor" }, { "id": "NFR-002", "statement": "The payment integration is isolated behind a single adapter module with no provider types leaking into domain code.", "ears_pattern": "n-a", "ears_pattern_na_reason": "architectural constraint, not a system response to a condition", "priority": "should", "verification_method": "architecture test (import boundary)" } ], "ears_violations": [] }
example.note: `verification_method` was suggested from `ears_pattern` (event → integration, unwanted → negative, ubiquitous → property/monitor) and then confirmed by a human. It is never auto-filled.
Four forbidden patterns at once: f3 (an FR may not opt out), f4 (no reason given), f5 (the statement emits E001/E008/W103/W111 and `ears_violations` was left empty anyway), f6 (`owner: team`).

section.title: Consistency rules the validator enforces
section.statement: `ears_pattern` MUST equal the pattern the linter derives from `statement` — a recorded classification that disagrees with the parser is a stale artefact, not an override. Every `E`-code the linter emits for a requirement MUST appear in `ears_violations` with the matching id; an empty `ears_violations` array asserts a clean parse and is checked, not trusted. `ears_pattern: n-a` requires `ears_pattern_na_reason` and an `NFR-` id.

text.reference: Contract validator and line linter; `--self-test` replays every fixture.
The rule table the validator loads. Same file the Go runtime embeds.
